items.text: A Hundred Spoons
Front Lobby

items.speaker: Dittarsdorf
items.text: Glad to have you here, old friend.
Dittarsdorf gets to his feet and extends a welcoming hand. This is the beginning of an amicable conversation.
His friend strides up to him and shakes his hand.

items.speaker: Dittarsdorf
items.text: Truth be told, I've considered many people for this job—many! But none suits the position better than you.

items.speaker: Dittarsdorf
items.text: You're being modest, my friend. I had thought about getting her a governess ...

items.speaker: Dittarsdorf
items.text: ... Governesses may well raise ordinary ladies, but my little girl is anything but. I'll settle for nothing but the very best for her.
"She must be virtuous, pure of thought, elegant, and compliant."
"She must be clever but guileless, talented yet modest, and dignified without pretension. Then, she will be a true noble lady."
... Heh heh.
Parents always have grand expectations for their children, don't they?
The child places a finger horizontally below her nose, mimicking a mustache as she speaks.
I'm a decent gentleman with impeccable manners. I never attend an event to which I am not invited.
I have a warm smile, a kind heart, and I never push others away. I have strong morals, respect social etiquette, and always present the best side of myself to others—when it's necessary.
Dittarsdorf regards me as a "true noble gentleman." He believes I possess every quality an honorable man should have.
The man maintains an upright posture, clasping his hands behind his back, his shoulders perfectly squared.
That's why, despite my eagerness to attend and the fact that I'm a family friend, I've never asked for, nor even hinted at wanting, an invitation to that banquet.
I know that asking is pointless. I must be patient.
When the time comes, the gate will be open to me.
The Dittarsdorf house is guarded by an enormous gate. It's beautiful and stately, made of metal, and artistically decorated with the family's motifs.
It's quite a feat, really—finding the balance between beauty and security.
And my friend Dittarsdorf has found that balance. His only lacking feature, of which he is fully aware, is the patience to educate a child.
He worries, you see—about a future in which his son is incompetent and chaotic and his daughter is crude and reckless. So, he's pinned his hopes on me.
The countenance of a middle-aged man faintly emerges on the girl's face. She licks her teeth—an unconscious display of greed.
Two figures in dresses emerge from the darkness and approach the gate. With a heavy rumble, it slides open.
Oh my. We've been talking all this time, yet we haven't so much as mentioned Isolde ...
She reaches out a hand and seizes your wrist. A gentle yet irresistible force leads you forward.
She should've been at the center of this conversation. So sweet and gentle—a truly thoughtful and beautiful girl.
She doesn't look back.
I treated her as my own. I taught her everything I knew, and she became that perfect young lady Dittarsdorf desired.
She was flawless. She met every expectation—from her mother, her father, her brother, the servants, and, of course, me.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Mind your posture, child.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Yes, Mr. Karl.
Little Isolde's body tenses. She straightens her back further.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Very well. Now lift your chin a little. No, not too high. We must avoid any indication of overconfidence.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: ... That's right. Just like that. Very well done, my child.
He lays his hands on the back of the chair in front of him and nods to his student on the other side of the hallway.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Alright, now maintain that posture and walk to me.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Yes, Mr. Karl.
It is rather premature for a girl of only twelve to learn to walk in 3-inch heels. But practicing now will avoid any future embarrassment.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Head up, shoulders square. Alright, now smooth strides. Don't sway, and don't bounce up and down.
Breathe in. Step forward, waist balanced. And again.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Don't lean forward. Straighten your back. Knees steady.
No mistakes. Don't make any mistakes.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: *exhales in relief*
She stops before the chair, awaiting her teacher's feedback.
Six years have passed. She's shot up since her first seance.
Her days of reaching up for door handles are long gone. She stands there, a living example of perfection—all thanks to her education.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Excellent, Isolde. Your walk is almost perfect now.
The gentleman smiles and pulls out the chair.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Have a seat. Let's move on to our next subject.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Time is against us, young lady. We spent an extra fifteen minutes working on your posture.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I've been told that you'll have a vocal lesson later. Don't worry, I shall see you again for our literature class after its completion.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Tonight we'll be reading about a dinner. There will be mention of the dining etiquette we've practiced before, so this is a good chance for you to review it.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... Certainly, Mr. Karl.
The girl gracefully sits down. A maid hurries over and helps her adjust the chair. A bowl of vegetable soup is sitting before her.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: May I ask a question, sir?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... If I remember correctly, you told me that we had completed the rules of dining etiquette last week. Did I misunderstand?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: You did not, my child.
The gentleman picks up a silver spoon and places it in her open palm. One by one, he adjusts her fingers until they close around the spoon handle.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: But last night, during dinner with your parents, I couldn't help but notice that your hands were shaking.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: The movements were subtle—almost imperceptible most of the time. You even hid them well while you cut the meat.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: When it came to the soup, however, the shaking was as clear as daylight. People will certainly notice your wetted cuffs.
With a smile on his face, Karl loosens his grip. Little Isolde needs no further instruction.
Her countenance is composed, yet her hand is trembling. Her fingertips turn pale as she tightens her grip on the spoon.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Of course, such a mistake wouldn't be considered rude, but it would reflect badly on your education.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: We've put in great effort and come so far. It would be a great shame to fall short on so small a detail.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Yes, Mr. Karl ... I'll work hard on it.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: A hundred times.
The gentleman paces around the lounge, feeling utterly complacent about his work.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I asked her to practice it a hundred times.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: She's the daughter of Evangeline, the greatest opera singer to ever grace the stages of Vienna. She has her eyes, her nose, her cheeks ... How could she possibly have such a shaky hand while using a spoon?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: What a disgrace.
He shakes his head, his dark hair on the back of his head shining with vitality.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I could tell she was getting tired towards the end of the session. She'd hidden it well thus far, just as she'd been instructed to do.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: She's only twelve, after all, and she went straight from a three-hour poise and posture class to repeatedly raising and lowering the spoon for an hour more.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: But she carried on. Just as I expected her to.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: She had a smile on her face. Her voice remained soft. Her eyes were gentle as a spring breeze. She's a darling little lamb.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: All our efforts paid off ...
He stops by the window. His gaze fixed upon the garden lawn.
Evangeline sits in the sunshine, a white rabbit in her arms. She's stroking it, gently grooming its hair.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Her wrists were still tight and shaky the first twenty times we practiced. It wasn't until the 65th attempt that things started to improve.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Perhaps she was too tired to shake; perhaps her joints were numb. Or perhaps she finally mastered the skill and calmed herself.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: By the 100th practice, the soup in her spoon was as still as a mirror. I could see the reflection of my face within it.
Karl's eyes flicker back to the table.
The soup is now cold and thick. The chair is pulled out, and Isolde is nowhere to be found.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I still have no idea why she was trembling so much. Maybe there's an issue with the muscles in her hand, or maybe it's an unfortunate side effect of her inherited ability.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: But I'm certain that she'll be rid of this unsightly habit within a week.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: She will become Evangeline, only better.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: This, you see, is the benefit of a proper education. If only I could travel back in time and give poor Evangeline the same opportunities ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: You seem surprised. Why?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I adore Evangeline. I'll forever be her loyal audience member and supportive friend. But that doesn't mean that I'm blind to her flaws.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: She's mad. Unstable. She spends half the day unconscious and the other half, God bless, in hysteria—even incontinence. She's a pitiful woman, indeed, worthy of little admiration.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Yes, she's the center of the crowd; yes, important figures attend her seances and listen to her piously; and yes, throngs of people cheer and throw flowers at her on stage, some even fainting from the excitement.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: But none of this speaks to who she truly is, my dear friend.
He shrugs.
The cold soup morphs into a slice of chocolate cake as he sits down at the table.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: You must be familiar with Sachertorte: two pieces of chocolate cake with a layer of apricot jam in the middle. It's the sweet embodiment of perfection.
With a silver fork in one hand, he flips the piece of cake on its side, revealing a moldy corner.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Evangeline is just like this cake. Most of her is sweet—her voice, her divination—but there's a rot growing that will one day devour her.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: It's still a little early to throw the cake away. That would be a shame—at least most of it still looks fine.
He cuts through the cake with his fork, precisely avoiding the molding edge.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: We can still enjoy the good part of the cake, as long as we're careful about where the dessert fork lands—Dittarsdorf did marry her, after all.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: But it's a somewhat troublesome process.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: The people's appetite for Sachertortes will never wane. And as one cake sours, they will look for another. Poor Evangeline simply cannot satisfy their desires any longer. They need something fresh, delicious, sweet ...
He savors the cake, a smile growing on his face.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Isolde is that new confectionary. Freshly out of the oven and waiting to be served.
TO BE CONTINUED…
